News.title: Woman, 23, found dead inside freezer by suspect’s girlfriend when pair were moving into house as man, 29, is arrested
News.content:
MYSTERY DEATH Woman, 23, found dead inside freezer by suspect’s girlfriend when pair were moving into house as man, 29, is arrested

A WOMAN’S frozen body has been found inside a freezer by a couple moving into a new home.

In a shocking twist, the suspect‘s girlfriend was reportedly the one to call cops after making the grim discovery on Sunday.





Manuela Vieira Matos Silva, 29, was found dead by a woman who was in the process of moving into the house, Globo reported.

The woman was reportedly looking for her boyfriend at their residence in Vitória da Conquista, Brazil, after she had not heard from him in days.

Once there, she noticed several items that weren’t hers and realised something was wrong.

After searching the home, she opened the freezer and shockingly found a body inside.



Cops rushed to the scene and confirmed it was Manuela who was reported missing on Friday.

She was reportedly last seen in the city centre talking to a man.

Lucas Santos Lima, 29, the boyfriend of the woman who discovered the body, was arrested on Monday.

Police are carrying at forensic investigations.



The Institute of Legal Medicine (IML) have not yet confirmed the cause of death.

It comes after a body has been found amid the hunt for a missing American Airlines flight attendant.

The grisly discovery was made in a rural area south of Medellín, Colombia, days after Eric Fernando Gutierrez Molina mysteriously disappeared.

Medellín Mayor Federico Gutiérrez announced the “sad news” in a post on X.

He wrote: “Since last Sunday, we have been searching for Eric Gutiérrez, a US citizen who is missing.



“Unfortunately, a lifeless body has just been found between the municipality of Jericó and Puente Iglesias. There is a very high probability that it is this person.”

The body, believed to be Molina’s, was transported to Medellín for identification and autopsy, according to the New York Post.

No suspects have been arrested in the discovery of the body and no cause of death has been revealed.

The 32-year-old crew member based in Dallas–Fort Worth, vanished while on an overnight stop in Medellín, according to officials.

News.title: Whitehall pen-pushers demand right to work from home due to Iran war
News.content:
WHITEHALL penpushers have demanded the right to work from home because of the Iran war.

The largest union representing civil servants urged ministers to ditch their mandatory office attendance rule of at least three days a week.





The Public and Commercial Services Union claimed the Middle East conflict was “pushing up costs for workers who are already struggling to make ends meet”.

It argued that commuting into work was “out of step” with the economic pressures bearing down on civil service households.

In a bid to justify its call, the PCS pointed to advice from the International Energy Agency (IEA), which recommends countries cut energy consumption by working from the sofa.

But the IEA plea from a fortnight ago was brushed aside by Sir Keir Starmer, whose spokesman said: “We [Britain] have a diverse and resilient supply.



“People in the UK should continue to go about their days in normal fashion.”

John O’Connell, chief executive of the TaxPayers’ Alliance, said: “The PCS claims that civil servants are poorly paid, despite Britain’s bureaucrats benefiting from higher salaries than their private sector counterparts on top of better holiday entitlements, more sick leave, and significantly more generous pensions.

“Ministers should be ignoring these demands and telling recalcitrant pen-pushers to grow up.”

News.title: Masonic lodge accused of running hit squads as 22 people – including spies – stand trial for murder of race car driver
News.content:
SECRET CLUB Masonic lodge accused of running hit squads as 22 people – including spies – stand trial for murder of race car driver

A FRENCH masonic lodge is at the centre of a murky trial as 22 people face a jury over murder and other serious crimes.

The pack of defendants appeared in court on Monday accused of carrying out the violent crimes on behalf of a mafia network inside the former Athanor Masonic Lodge.





Prosecutors allege the lodge served as a hub for a tightly organised network that carried out violent acts ranging from assaults to contract killings.

Thirteen of the 22 defendants face life imprisonment.

The group has been accused of murdering a racing driver, the attempted murder of a business coach and a trade unionist, aggravated assault and criminal conspiracy.



Most of the accused, aged between 30 and 73, have no previous criminal record.

Several members of the freemasons lodge – located in the Parisian suburb of Puteaux – have appeared in the dock.

Four military personnel from France’s foreign intelligence service (DGSE), two police officers, a retired domestic intelligence officer, a security guard, a doctor, an engineer and two business executives make up the group of defendants.

The alleged ringleaders have been identified as Athanor freemasons Jean-Luc Bagur, Frédéric Vaglio and Daniel Beaulieu.



If they are convicted, they face life in prison.

Sébastien Leroy, Beaulieu’s right-hand man, also faces life in prison.

He was not a member of the lodge.

Leroy has been accused of carrying out the trio’s dirty work himself, or through a network of hitmen.

A botched contract killing in July 2020 led police to uncover the network, when two members of the military were arrested in possession of weapons near the home of business coach Marie-Hélène Dini.



They told police during questioning that they had been asked to murder Dini on behalf of the French state.

According to the suspects, they were told she was working for the Israeli spy agency, the Mossad.

Investigators then unearthed a link to Bagur, 69, who was a rival business coach to Dini and the “venerable master” of the Athanor lodge.

Bagur allegedly asked fellow freemason Vaglio to arrange for his rival to be killed, offering to pay a fee of £60,843 (€70,000).



Vaglio, a 53-year-old entrepreneur, faces accusations of working as the intermediary between the big boss and a hit squad working for fellow Athanor freemason Beaulieu.

Beaulieu is a 72-year-old retired agent for the domestic intelligence service (DGSI).

The leader of the hit squad, Leroy, told cops he or his associates carried out most of the assaults, robberies and murders for the Athanor mafia, including the 2018 killing of racing car driver Laurent Pasquali.



His body was found in a forest after he allegedly failed to pay a debt to one of Vaglio’s friends.

Crimes ordered by the organised crime group escalated with time, beginning as petty revenge attacks and escalating to homicide, according to the investigation.

One of the charges relating to industrial espionage alleged that Leroy’s gang assaulted a businesswoman in the street and snatched her computer.

In 2019, the car of one of Bagur’s associates was set on fire after she found evidence of financial fraud within his company.

Leroy, a security guard, told investigators he was under the impression he had been acting on behalf of the French government.



He claimed Beaulieu had “manipulated” him using the idea of him becoming an informant for the DGSI domestic spy agency.

Jean-William Vezinet, lawyer for the targeted business coach Dini, said his client had been “terrified” that “people who are supposed to act for the good of society” were the key figures in the crime.

It remains unclear what evidence the prosecution has gathered from their interviews with Beaulieu, the accused ringleader.

He allegedly made an attempt to commit suicide in police custody.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The attempt has left him disabled with “impaired concentration”, according to his lawyer.



The trial is slated to run for a minimum of three months.

News.title: Lift fracking ban, approve North Sea oil & build coal-fired power stations… how Labour SHOULD be tackling fuel crisis
News.content:
ALL governments have a tendency to blame anyone but themselves for their errors, but this one has raised it to a fine art.

Yesterday, the Prime Minister hosted a meeting of oil companies in Downing Street to discuss the crisis in Iran and how consumers can be protected.





It follows days in which government ministers have tried to put it about that the reason fuel prices are so high is down to “price gouging” on the part of retailers.

Meanwhile, Rachel Reeves and Ed Miliband headed off to a meeting of G7 finance and energy ministers to lecture them that the way out of the current crisis is to accelerate the switch to renewables, so that we can all exit the “fossil fuel rollercoaster”.

Obviously, the immediate cause of the current crisis is Donald Trump’s decision to attack Iran without putting in much thought as to how the global economy would cope if — as was surely predictable — Iran started attacking shipping in the Straits of Hormuz, through which 20 per cent of the world’s oil supply has to pass.

But there are reasons why UK consumers have been left especially vulnerable to this crisis, and it has nothing to do with “profiteering” on the part of oil companies, supermarkets or anyone else.



It is because the present Government has been doggedly pursuing an energy policy which puts the attainment of Net Zero above all else.

Why the Chancellor and Energy Secretary think that other countries will do anything but snort with derision at being invited to copy the example of Britain is anyone’s guess.

The building spree in wind and solar farms has done nothing to protect us against the fallout from the Iran War, but it has helped give us the highest electricity prices of any member country of the International Energy Agency.

We don’t have a national energy security policy worthy of the name. If we did, sure, it would include some “home-grown” wind and solar.



But these two sources of energy account for just five per cent of our overall energy use, while fossil fuels account for three quarters of it. There is no chance of this changing rapidly in the foreseeable future.

Anyone looking at it from anything other than an ideological perspective could see that the overwhelming priority for the Government at the moment should be to maximise supplies of home-grown fossil fuels.

Yet the Government refuses to do this — in spite of even the renewables industry itself telling Miliband he should lift his ban on new North Sea licences.

Not only that, the Government should be repealing the ban on fracking so that we can exploit the estimated half a century’s worth of gas which lies below the British mainland.

Cuadrilla Resources — which has previously sunk wells in Lancashire but was forced to abandon them when the previous government introduced a moratorium on fracking — said at the weekend that it could get gas supplies up and running in three months if given the chance.



That, crucially, would be in time for next winter.

We would be in a much better position, too, had the Government not closed the last coal-fired power station in 2024.

At the time the closure was hailed as a huge breakthrough for the environment, and sure enough coal is a dirty fuel which we might not want to use too much of in normal times.

But what closing that power station has done is to deprive us of a very reliable baseload of power without having to rely on gas.



As we found out 40 years ago, when the Thatcher government managed to keep the lights on for 11 months of the miners’ strike, one advantage of coal is that it is very easy to stockpile.

As for blaming petrol retailers for “price gouging” — a term used by Miliband as well as by Education Secretary Bridget Phillipson over the weekend — it is a disgrace.

Sure, it is possible to find garages, especially at motorway service stations, which are selling fuel at way over the odds.

But a report by the Competition and Markets Authority last December found that the average profit margin for petrol retailers was around ten per cent.

That is not huge. If you want private companies to provide a vital public service like supplying us with fuel, while bearing the financial risks, they have to be able to earn a reasonable return on capital.



This is ignored by far too many Labour politicians who seem to think that any level of profit is immoral.

That profits pay the pensions of millions of private pensioners who don’t have taxpayer-funded pensions goes straight over their heads.

Retailers can’t help that Reeves plans to raise fuel duty by five pence a litre over the next year, nor that business rates are going up, nor that the minimum wage and Employment Rights Act is adding to their costs.

How much easier it is to blame nasty capitalists rather than look at your own policies.

Sorry, but it won’t wash.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

While our own Government did not launch the strikes on Iran, it is very much to blame for policies that overlook national energy security and which are driving up consumer prices on all fronts.

News.title: High street giant with 320 shops plots 'huge wave of closures' in latest blow
News.content:
A leading UK high street retailer is planning a 'huge wave of closures' as part of a major shake-up.

The budget chain, Poundstretcher, could shut numerous sites across its 320-strong store estate if a proposed restructuring plan gets the go-ahead.

According to reports, the overhaul could commence within days. Sky News reported that the firm is collaborating with advisers on a court-sanctioned, creditor-approved restructuring plan.

The discount chain was acquired by Fortress Investment Group two years ago, reports the Express. It remains uncertain how many of the almost 320 operational stores will shut as a consequence.

Industry insiders are suggesting that the strategy would probably include rent reduction requests from multiple landlords. The chain was established in 1981 and is one of the UK's premier discount retailers.

Image: Elena Demetriou) Elena Demetriou)

In April 2024, it was sold by businessman Aziz Tayub, who had owned the business for 18 years, and approximately 4,000 people were employed.

The anticipated closures arrive as the UK High Street faces a crisis, with over 13,000 shops closing last year, and experts cautioning that further casualties are expected, with some of the nation's largest retailers affected.

A significant proportion of the High Street shops disappearing this year have been run by fashion retailers, including the likes of New Look and Quiz.

Other retailers shutting stores include WHSmith and Homebase.

News.title: George Michael's jacket and Slash's guitar among iconic musical items up for sale
News.content:
George Michael's jacket and Slash's guitar among iconic musical items up for sale

The guitar is among 400 lots available for worldwide bidding, with a combined pre-sale estimate of £1.5 million, including treasures belonging to George Michael, Sir Paul McCartney and Amy Winehouse

View 4 Images The leather jacket George Michael wore in the video for his 1987 hit Faith is going under the hammer for as much as £120,000 (Image: Propstore/Cover Images)

The guitar used by Slash of Guns N' Roses during the chart-topping rock group's Not In This Lifetime tour is expected to fetch as much as £300,000 when it is offered at auction.

‌



The photo-matched, stage-used and autographed Gibson Les Paul `59 Custom Shop guitar was played during the US band's 2016 tour, which saw Axl Rose, Slash and Duff McKagan reunite for the first time since 1993. The instrument, which carries an estimate of £150,000 to £300,000, is due to go under the hammer at Propstore auction house in London next month as part of the Music Memorabilia Live Auction collection.

‌



A jacket worn by the late George Michael during the music video for his 1987 hit single Faith is also up for sale, and hopes to fetch between £60,000 and £120,000. The Grammy-winning artist, known for hits including Father Figure and One More Try, also wore the jacket onstage during his Faith tour in 1998.

‌



US World Cup stadium was sold for £400k after being abandoned and criticised by England boss READ MORE :

Ex-England and Man Utd ace forced to sell memorabilia after working as a postman READ MORE :

View 4 Images The guitar played during Guns N' Roses’ Not In This Lifetime tour - the first reunion tour featuring Axl Rose, Slash and Duff McKagan since 1993 (Image: Propstore/Cover Images)

The auction is taking place on April 30 and will also include a gold microphone presented to rock band Queen and used by frontman Freddie Mercury, which expects to sell for £30,000 to £60,000. The microphone is part of a collection belonging to Peter Hince, the band's head roadie and auction consignor, who said he has "wonderful memories" working with the best-selling group.

He added: "I'm pleased to be offering (these items) through Propstore, where they can now be shared with fans and collectors who appreciate what they represent in Queen's story." Also up for sale is an autographed large-format promotional poster for John Lennon and Yoko Ono's Double Fantasy, signed by the former Beatles singer hours before his death in 1980, aged 40.

‌



View 4 Images Also up for grabs is Paul McCartney’s Handwritten “Goodbye” First-Draft Lyrics which could fetch up to £110,000 at auction (Image: Propstore/Cover Images)

The item is expected to fetch between £60,000 and £120,000 and is up for sale alongside handwritten lyrics to Goodbye written by Lennon's bandmate, Sir Paul McCartney, which dates to 1969 and is expected to fetch £55,000 to £110,000.

Other items up for sale include a Fred Perry trench coat belonging to the late Amy Winehouse — which has a pre-sale estimate of £4,000 to £8,000 — and an autographed jacket worn by singer Ed Sheeran in his Shape Of You music video, which is expected to sell for between £3,500 and £7,000.

‌



The event will offer more than 400 lots available for worldwide bidding, with a combined pre-sale estimate of £1.5 million. Mark Hochman, Propstore music specialist, said: "Propstore's upcoming Music Live Auction brings together some of the most influential names in popular music, from legends such as The Beatles, Queen, George Michael and Jimi Hendrix to modern global stars including Ed Sheeran and Little Mix.

View 4 Images Slash's autographed Gibson Les Paul '59 Custom Shop guitar was played during the US band's 2016 tour is up for auction (Image: PA)

"Featuring stage-used instruments, handwritten lyrics and iconic performance-worn pieces — including over 60 items from the personal collection of Queen head roadie Peter Hince — the sale spans genres, generations and defining cultural moments.

Article continues below

"Each lot offers collectors a tangible connection to the artists and performances that helped shape the soundtrack of our lives."

News.title: 'The BBC must quickly get a grip or risk damaging confidence further'
News.content:
'The BBC must quickly get a grip or risk damaging confidence further'

Repeated crises at one of Britain's most trusted institutions suggest deeper problems behind the scenes at the BBC - audiences expect better and deserve transparency

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Scott Mills' departure from Radio 2 is another headache the BBC could do without

Another BBC star, another messy exit, another reputational headache the corporation could well do without.

Scott Mills’ sudden departure from Radio 2, first revealed by the Mirror, leaves more questions than answers and adds to a growing list of controversies that continue to chip away at public trust.

For an organisation funded by licence fee payers, this is becoming an uncomfortable pattern. Mills was no bit-part player. He was one of the BBC’s highest-paid stars, reportedly earning between £355,000 and £359,999 a year and had only recently stepped into the flagship Radio 2 breakfast slot.

Stability and familiarity were promised. Instead, listeners have been left in the dark. The BBC’s tight-lipped response will only fuel speculation.

But the wider issue is clear: repeated crises suggest deeper problems behind the scenes. Audiences expect better and deserve transparency. The BBC must get a grip on these situations quickly, or risk further damaging confidence in one of Britain’s most trusted institutions.

Scrapping non-hate crime incidents is disrespectful and dangerous

Scrapping the recording of non-crime hate incidents would be a shameful step backwards. Stephen Lawrence’s murder forced Britain to confront institutional racism and led to hard-won reforms that put victims at the heart of policing.

To quietly row back now, without even consulting his father, is both disrespectful and dangerous. Neville Lawrence is right to be alarmed.

If incidents are not recorded, they are not seen. And if they are not seen, they are not stopped. These records are not bureaucracy; they are early warnings.

Article continues below

They help police understand patterns, protect communities and prevent escalation. Abandoning them sends the worst possible message: that prejudice can go unchecked. After everything learned since 1993, we cannot afford to go backwards.

Tribute to a man of love, pride and resilience

Geoff Burrow’s life was defined by love, pride and resilience. He stood by his son Rob through his brave, heartbreaking battle with MND, showing the same strength that inspired a nation.

Fittingly, he lived to see his son named Super League’s greatest half-back of the last 30 years - a legacy that rightly will endure.

News.title: Major bin rule changes in full as new laws come into effect from today
News.content:
Major bin rule changes in full as new laws come into effect from today

The Government's Simpler Recycling scheme, which has been long in the works, is set to extend to households this week, ending a 'postcode lottery' for recycling in England

View 5 Images The Simpler Recycling scheme will activate for households from March 31 (Image: inyourArea)

A set of new bin rules comes into effect today as the Government rolls out its Simpler Recycling scheme to British homes, a year after the scheme was introduced.

‌



Labour launched the recycling scheme under the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) in 2025, aiming to streamline waste collections in England initially for businesses, requiring glass, metal, plastic, paper and card to be collected separately from general waste.

‌



The initiative is designed to boost British recycling, with observance having fallen in recent years, initially just for businesses but now for regular households.

‌



Local authorities will implement standardised core recycling collections from today, with the new rules set to make recycling easier for millions of people.

Bin rule changes that will affect all households in England this April READ MORE :

Lawyer explains what to do if neighbours break new March 31 bin rules READ MORE :

View 5 Images The new rules are intended to streamline the country's recycling system (Image: Getty)

How refuse will be divided - all the bins

The new rules will require Brit households to divide waste between four separate bins, separating out food with paper, card, recyclables and general rubbish.

‌



The bins include:

Food and Garden Waste

Paper and Card

Dry Recyclables (Glass, Metal, Plastic)

General Rubbish

Full list of items refuse collectors don't take

Brits should make a note of the kinds of materials that cannot be deposited in standard household recycling, as DEFRA advises refuse collectors that there are materials "you do not need to collect" under the Simpler Recycling scheme. These include several items many people might otherwise assume can be disposed with their typical waste.

‌



According to DEFRA, the items that can't be collected include:

Glass

Candles

Drinking glasses

Flat glass

Glass cookware (such as Pyrex)

Light bulbs and tubes

Microwave plates

Mirrors

Vases

Window glass

Ceramics, such as crockery or earthenware

‌



View 5 Images Not every type of material can be recycled under the new rules (Image: PA)

Metal

Laminated foil, like pet food pouches and coffee pouches

Electrical items and batteries

General kitchenware like cutlery, pots and pans

Kettles

Irons

Pipes

Metal packaging that has contained white spirits, paints, engine oils or antifreeze

‌



Plastic

Any plastic packaging or non-packaging items labelled as 'compostable' or 'biodegradable’, including coffee pods

Plastic bottles that have contained white spirits, paints, engine oils or antifreeze

Bulky rigid plastics such as garden furniture, bins and plastic toys

Polystyrene (expanded and high impact) packaging such as packing beads

Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) packaging

Paper and card

‌



Food and drinks cartons made of a fibre-based composite (these should be collected in the plastic stream)

Absorbent hygiene products (AHPs) including nappies, period products and incontinence products

Cotton wool or makeup pads

Tissue or toilet paper

Wet wipes

Food waste

Any plastic packaging or non-packaging items labelled as 'compostable' or 'biodegradable', including coffee pods

Garden waste

Animal bedding

Bulky waste (including garden furniture and fencing)

Garden tools or other gardening equipment

Plant pots

Plastic

Sand

Sawdust

Stone, gravel or bricks

Tea bags or coffee grounds

Branches and trees over a certain size may have to be cut into smaller pieces to follow local guidance

‌



View 5 Images There are some limited civil fines for people who break bin rules (Image: Michael Nguyen/NurPhoto/REX/Shutterstock)

How the new rules will be enforced

There are no strict new enforcement rules to come with the Simpler Recycling changes, but Brits can still be stuck with fines for "incorrect presentation of household waste" in England.

This is a civil penalty and can result in the issuance of a Fixed Penalty Notice, worth between £60 and £80, but only after a written warning is provided, and where incorrect presentation "is causing a nuisance".

‌



How to ensure you don't break the rules

The major rule change could bring about an all-new order of neighbour disputes, with the number of new bins causing confusion among households. And it could cause further issues with local councils, who, experts have warned, may "refuse to collect" any rubbish deemed "contaminated".

Simarjot Singh Judge, managing partner at Judge Law, said: “Where recycling systems become more complex, there is always a risk of disputes arising, particularly if one household’s actions affect others."

Mr Judge added: “If a bin is contaminated, councils can refuse to collect it, which can impact not just one household but others nearby.” The situation could result in tensions between residents and the local council, with the lawyer adding that neighbours could raise complaints, "particularly if they feel someone else’s behaviour is affecting their service".

‌



Mr Judge said that the best approach to preventing rulebreaking is to stay up-to-date with local guidance and take extra care when sorting waste.

View 5 Images The Government says the new rules will end the 'postcode lottery' of recycling (Image: WalesOnline/Rob Browne)

What the Government says

The Government has said the new rules will end what it calls a "postcode lottery" impacting the country with a set of universal rules across England. Councils have previously placed different rules locally for what materials refuse collectors will take from households in their areas.

Article continues below

A DEFRA spokesperson said: Citizens will be able to recycle the same materials across England, whether at home, work or school, and will no longer need to check what is accepted for recycling in their local area.

“A universal standard will ensure that everything that can be collected for household recycling is collected in every region. Simpler Recycling will also end the ‘postcode lottery’ of bin collections in England, whereby councils collect different materials for recycling, causing confusion for households.”

News.title: UK weather maps show Easter bank holiday scorcher as 4 regions to bake in 17C on Saturday
News.content:
UK weather maps show Easter bank holiday scorcher as 4 regions to bake in 17C on Saturday

The Easter bank holiday is set to see some warmth after a colder snap with some areas in the UK welcoming a scorching 17C on Saturday according to new weather maps

View 2 Images Temperatures will reach 17C on Saturday according to WXCharts (Image: WXCharts )

New weather maps show temperatures heating up over the bank holiday as the nation can expect some sunshine this weekend.

‌



Brits will see highs of 17C on Saturday, April 4 according to maps from WXCharts, which uses MetDesk data.

‌



Warmer temperatures are predicted in the south and east, with the early evening set to be the warmest time of day.

‌



View 2 Images Temperatures are expected to be slightly cooler at midday (Image: WXCharts )

At 12pm, London will reach 15C with areas in northern England remaining slightly colder. As the day closes, the warmth will continue, with Cambridgeshire welcoming 17C at 6pm.

The warmer spell is predicted after a colder snap with drizzly conditions towards the end of the week.

‌



According to the Met Office: "The wettest and windiest weather is more likely towards the west and north of the country. Beyond Easter, a broad northwest-southeast split is most likely, though the extent of high pressure into southern areas is unclear.

"That said, northern and western parts are more likely to remain rather unsettled overall, with further spells of wind and rain, and areas further southeast should see the best of the drier, clearer interludes.

"Temperatures probably fairly close to average overall, but occasional warmer spells are possible in the south."

Article continues below

On Saturday the south will see the warmer temperatures with several regions forecast sunshine. In the East Midlands temperatures are also heating up, with Nottingham and Derby anticipating 16C, according to the maps.

Regions that can expect 17C

Hertfordshire

Bedfordshire

Cambridgeshire

Lincolnshire

In the North, Manchester will reach 14C at 6pm with Yorkshire forecast to hit 15C. The unexpected temperatures come after the country was expected to see a colder snap over the weekend, particularly in Scotland and northern England.

News.title: Brits dealt ANOTHER weather blow as maps show -6C ice blast to hit UK
News.content:
Brits dealt ANOTHER weather blow as maps show -6C ice blast to hit UK

The latest weather forecast maps show a bitter cold front descending over the UK over the next few days, with snowfall coming hand-in-hand as the country should be warming up

View 4 Images Weather maps show a deep freeze descending on the UK (Image: WXCHARTS)

Brits have been dealt another weather blow as the latest weather map show an incoming wintry freeze just a few days before the long Easter weekend.

‌



Forecasts across the country have ranged from grey and wet to bright and cold as the typical temperate back-and-forth of spring continues. Temperatures have remained broadly in the mid-to-high single figures in the morning, before reaching into the teens in the afternoon, around the average for the time of year.

‌



But maps suggest the mercury could nosedive in the days to come, plunging as low as -6C, even causing snow during what should be the warmest times of day.

‌



Met Office weather forecast names UK areas facing snow within hours READ MORE :

View 4 Images Maps show temperatures from the day before the severe cold reaching into the teens (Image: WXCHARTS)

The latest maps from WXCharts show a cold blast approaching from the northwest this coming week, with the mercury sliding down nearly 20C in total.

While highs of 14C are possible in the UK today, come tomorrow, they could drop into the minus range. Charts show the cold blast gripping the Scottish coast from 6am on April 1, gradually driving temperatures down over the following few hours to -2C over the Highlands that evening.

‌



By 12am on April 2, the cold will deepen still, bringing temperatures down to -4C on the west coast, and -5C and -6C further east, with the chill eventually covering the entire home nation by 12pm.

View 4 Images The forecast also shows some snow descending on Scotland (Image: WXCHARTS)

As the severe cold takes shape above Scotland, so too will snow, winter weather maps from the same provider, which uses data from MetDesk, suggest. The Scottish Highlands will bear the vast brunt of the snowfall, which will only last until around 6pm that day, and pour out less than an inch in total.

‌



The long-range weather forecast, which covers April 4 to 13, states that the weather will remain unpredictable through the remainder of the Easter break .

But the forecast states there is an added possibility of "occasional warmer spells", likely confined to the typically hotter parts of the country. The agency said: "It is increasingly likely that unsettled conditions will affect the UK over the Easter Holiday weekend, with the potential for strong winds and heavy rain at times."

View 4 Images The deep chill will descend over Scotland from Tuesday (Image: WXCHARTS)

Article continues below

"The wettest and windiest weather is more likely towards the west and north of the country. Beyond Easter, a broad northwest-southeast split is most likely, though the extent of high pressure into southern areas is unclear.

"That said, northern and western parts are more likely to remain rather unsettled overall, with further spells of wind and rain, and areas further southeast should see the best of the drier, clearer interludes. Temperatures probably fairly close to average overall, but occasional warmer spells are possible in the south."

News.title: Tourist dies after being buried under avalanche during skiing trip in Austria
News.content:
Tourist dies after being buried under avalanche during skiing trip in Austria

Tragedy struck when Federico Giubilato and a friend went skiing off-piste at Marchkopf, Austria, as an 820ft-wide avalanche left them buried under heaps of snow

View 4 Images Federico Giubilato died after he was buried in an avalanche (Image: Jam Press)

A tourist has tragically died after being buried in an avalanche in Austria.

‌



Federico Giubilato, who would have turned 42 yesterday, was trapped under the 820ft-wide avalanche on Saturday with his friend. His 36-year-old pal managed to break free with just a hand injury and alerted emergency services.

‌



But despite best efforts of authorities, Federico, from Bassano del Grappa, in northern Italy, was declared dead. He and his mate had been skiing off-piste during a trip to Marchkopf, Austria when tragedy struck on Saturday afternoon, a horror which echoed a further avalanche elsewhere this month in which another man died.

‌



Federico was an extreme sports enthusiast, with images posted on his social media showing the young man enjoying downhill mountain biking, surfing, climbing, and other pursuits. However, the engineer suffered a serious injury in 2019 and spent more than two years recovering.

Horror avalanche kills 2 and sweeps 10 away as major search and rescue launched READ MORE :

View 4 Images Federico loved nature and outdoor adventures (Image: Jam Press)

During Saturday's ordeal, Federico and his friend were trapped under around 5.2ft (1.6m) of ice. The pal, who has not been named, miraculously broke free and alerted emergency services.

‌



But the mountain rescue team arrived in two helicopters about half an hour later. It took a further 30 minutes to dig Federico out, it is understood. By this time, the university graduate had died.

Federico, who was a mechanical engineer, was particularly passionate about mountaineering. When, though, he hurt himself in an extreme sports accident in 2019, Federico wrote online: "Events sometimes happen with unimaginable speed: in a fraction of a second, you make a mistake, you realise your error, you try to correct it, you realise the attempt to correct it is futile, you hit the ground running, you feel your body no longer responding, the worst thoughts invade your brain, you're back to square one.

"Time expands and contracts, demonstrating the relativity of its perception. The push comes from within, the desire to go back to doing what makes me feel alive. The push comes from the waves of affection from those around me."

‌



4 View 4 Images The engineer was skiing off-piste when tragedy struck (Image: Jam Press) 4 View 4 Images Tributes have been paid to Federico, who was from Italy

The tragedy in Marchkopf, which is near Hochfügen, part of the larger Zillertal ski region, follows another deadly avalanche. Kai Smart, 23, was caught in this disaster in Japan earlier this month. It left Kai in a coma, from which he sadly did not recover.

Article continues below

The man's dad, John, posted on Instagram: "It is with immense sadness that we have to let you know that our kind, brave and beautiful son and brother Kai is no longer with us. We are beyond heartbroken and there are no words to describe the pain we are feeling losing him so young.

"Kai was a warrior, a mountain man, an explorer of the world, a lover of people of all walks of life, an inspiration to so many, an honour student, a passionate skier, surfer, dirt biker, climber, kitesurfer and so much more."

News.title: Dad uttered four terrifying final words in call to police before wife did unthinkable
News.content:
Dad uttered four terrifying final words in call to police before wife did unthinkable

Collin Turner phoned the police after claiming he had been locked in the garage by his wife Bree Kuhn but during the call he uttered his last ever four words after he was murdered in cold blood

View 3 Images Bree Kuhn remains behind bars (Image: Santa Rosa County Jail)

A father called 911 to report having been locked in the garage by his wife — before he uttered four chilling words as gunshots suddenly blasted out.

‌



It is approaching five years since Collin Turner was heard saying his heartbreaking last words and below we look back at his senseless murder.

‌



Colin, who had served in the US Marines for 14 years, lived with his wife, Bree Kuhn, at their home in Gulf Breeze, Florida. They lived together with their two children, then three and four, along with Kuhn’s third child from a previous relationship.

‌



Kuhn, meanwhile, was a US Navy chief petty officer. On September 8, 2021, police were called out to their home on multiple occasions and the chilling case was recently explored in an episode of Coffeehouse Crime.

It was reported that Collin, who was by then a stay at home dad and an electrical engineering student, wanted to take the children to his parents home — but Kuhn was against the idea.

View 3 Images Collin Turner was just 33 when he lost his life (Image: watersandhibbert.com)

‌



She initially called the Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office shortly before 1pm but cops found no evidence of anything physical between the married couple. Collin, 33, meanwhile called at 5pm but again officers left the home after asking the pair questions.

However, at around 6.22pm, Collin again called 911, and he said: “Hi, you guys have been out to my house twice today. And then most recently, the deputy talked to my wife into letting me into the house and then she locked me in the garage and like, tried to break my arm when I was trying to get back inside.”

Collin was then asked for his address, which he provided, before he went on: “She’s currently got me locked in the garage because she broke both of our big doors and then she… But I came out here to fix it after getting in the house earlier, she locked the door behind me. Then when I said…”

‌



At this moment, a gunshot suddenly erupted before a scream was heard. The dispatcher asked: “What was that? What was that?”

Audibly terrified, Collin then spoke his last ever words, as he chillingly said: “She just shot me!” More gunshots were then sounded — and Collin was left dead in a pool of his own blood.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Kuhn was soon arrested and while she admitted to having shot her husband, she claimed she acted in self-defence. In a teary police interview, she said: “I told him that I wanted a divorce so he was just trying to take the kids.”

Asked what happened to Collin, she said “I don’t remember” before she added: “I didn’t mean to shoot him. It was at least twice. I didn’t mean to shoot him… he said something and just the look on his face, he was like…”

He was then asked what the look was, before she replied: “He was going to kill me.”

‌



During her murder trial, Kuhn’s attorney told the court: “He [Collin] had threatened to kill these kids before, and her as well. She was worried he was going to take the kids and kill them.” However, prosecutors said there was “no verification, documentation of any of these allegations”.

View 3 Images She shot her own husband to death (Image: Santa Rosa County Jail)

Kuhn was found guilty of premeditated first-degree murder and in September 2024 was sentenced to life behind bars. She showed no emotion when the verdict was delivered before Collin’s mother read out a devastating victim impact statement.

Article continues below

She said: “When I think of the impact the loss of Collin has made on my life. It is difficult to put into words. The grief can wash over at any time. Our daughters have had the shock of unexpectedly losing their brother. And as a mother, their pain is my pain. But the greatest impact has been watching how this loss has impacted Collin’s younger children.

“We have custody of them and expect to raise them for the rest of our lives. It's been three years and they’re still fearful that we will die and leave them once again without parents. They worry that if we bicker, one of us may kill the other. They still ask if we have guns in the house, though they know the answer is no. No matter how many times we remind them that killing a loved one is very rare, their reality tells them differently.”
